why: The first recursive tree function: a node's depth is 1 + the larger depth of its two subtrees, and an empty tree has depth 0. Every DFS that returns a value from the children is this shape.
hints: Suppose someone hands you the depths of the left and right subtrees. What is the depth of the whole tree?
depth(None) = 0; depth(node) = 1 + max(depth(node.left), depth(node.right)). The recursion visits every node once.
Write it recursively first. For a 100000-node chain, switch to an explicit stack of (node, depth) pairs and keep the largest depth seen. O(n) time.
pitfalls: Depth counts nodes, not edges: a single node has depth 1.
A skewed tree of 100000 nodes overflows Python's recursion limit; use a stack or raise the limit.
